\begin{proof}[Proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:intrinsic-annular}]
\proves{prop:intrinsic-annular}
Put $\kappa=\sqrt{\max(K,1)}$ and
$q=\min\{r/2,1/(2\kappa)\}$. Jacobi comparison supplies a
uniform positive normal radius. Choose $h$ smaller than this
radius and $q/100$, and choose $\mu$ smaller than both
$(1-\delta)^2h(q/10)$ and $1/(100\kappa^2)$.

Normal rays cannot be treated as an embedded collar in advance.
At an earliest collision inside a specified region, shorten the
base-to-vertex minimizers and keep their interiors in that region.
The confined radial family bounds the length of its focusing
arc by the turning of the boundary segment. Regional descent
then excludes central returns and long two-sided regions.

Choose the retained strips cyclically rather than starting from an
arbitrary cut of the first boundary. The return and collision
arguments discard at most $L_0/50$ and $3L_0/50$. Injectivity of the
remaining normal strips makes their areas disjoint. The small-area
hypothesis discards fewer than $L_0/10$ additional bases whose
normal rays have not reached the opposite boundary by height $h$.
Thus a retained set $Z$ has length greater than $41L_0/50$.
Its endpoint map to the opposite boundary is injective and
stretches arclength by at least $1-\delta$. Hence
\[
 L_1\geq(1-\delta)|Z|>
       (99/100)(41/50)L_0>3L_0/4.
\]
\end{proof}
